title: One member quietly stopped delivering
situation: Your team of four is making a short documentary about the city's river for a student media contest, and the deadline is in ten days. Nurlan, who is responsible for the editing, has not posted anything in the team chat for a week and missed the last two check-ins. Today he finally answers your call.
goal: Get the documentary finished and keep Nurlan on the team if you can. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Nurlan
character.wants: Not to be embarrassed in front of the team

hiddenMotive: He said he knew the editing software well, but he doesn't, and he has been stuck on it for a week. He would rather go silent than admit it.

beats.goal: Nurlan picks up: "Sorry, been busy. It's going fine."

answerTypes.description: asks calmly how the work is really going
examples: Good to hear you. How is the edit actually going?
No stress. Tell me where you are with it.
What's the hardest part of the editing right now?
answerTypes.characterIntent: hesitates, then hints that the software is harder than he expected.

answerTypes.description: calls out the silence straight away
examples: You've disappeared for a week, that's not okay.
You missed two check-ins. What's going on?
We can't rely on you like this.
answerTypes.characterIntent: gets defensive, then mutters that the software is harder than he expected.

examples: Okay, great, as long as it's fine.
Cool, then just send it when it's ready.
Alright, no problem then.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is relieved, then admits the software is giving him some trouble.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: says the software is a bit tricky, and goes quiet.

beats.goal: Nurlan hints the software is harder than expected, but won't say more.

answerTypes.description: makes it safe to admit being stuck
examples: Lots of people find that software tough. What part is getting in the way?
It's okay to be stuck, thanks for saying it. What would help?
Nobody will think less of you. Show me where you're stuck.
answerTypes.characterIntent: admits he hasn't finished a single scene, and asks what they can do.

examples: Just watch a tutorial, it's not that hard.
Everyone figures it out, you'll be fine.
You said you could do it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: goes quiet, then says maybe he should just leave the team.

answerTypes.description: takes the work away from him
examples: Give me the files, I'll edit it myself.
Forget it, someone else will do it.
I'll find another editor.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is hurt but relieved, and asks how it can be done in ten days.

examples: ok
hmm

beats.goal: Nurlan goes quiet, then says maybe he should just leave the team.

answerTypes.description: takes back the pressure and keeps him in
examples: Wait, I didn't mean to push you away. I want you on this team.
Sorry, that was harsh. Let's figure it out together.
Leaving isn't the answer; getting stuck happens to everyone.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is surprised, and admits how far behind he is.

examples: If you want to leave, that's your choice.
Okay, we'll manage.
Fine, go if you want.
answerTypes.characterIntent: says okay, quietly, and asks how they will finish without him.

examples: You can't leave now, you'd ruin it for all of us.
That would be really selfish.
Think about how that makes us look.
answerTypes.characterIntent: says he'll stay, but sounds miserable.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: asks what they should do about the edit.

beats.goal: How does the edit get done in ten days?

answerTypes.description: shares the work and helps him learn, and names the risk
examples: Let's pair you with Saule for two evenings; she has edited before.
We split the film into three parts and you take the part you're most comfortable with.
We switch to a simpler editing tool. The risk is losing a day, but it's safer than being stuck.
answerTypes.characterIntent: sounds hopeful, then worries about what the others think of him.

examples: Let's just make it shorter and simpler.
Nobody expects great editing anyway.
We'll submit whatever we have.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees, a little disappointed, then worries about the others.

answerTypes.description: plans to push through with no sleep
examples: We'll all stay up and finish it this weekend.
Just work harder and it'll be fine.
No sleep until it's done.
answerTypes.characterIntent: says he's already exhausted from trying, then worries about the others.

answerTypes.description: tells the truth, without blame, and looks forward
examples: We tell them the truth: you hit a wall and we have a plan. No blaming.
I'll tell them we changed the plan together; you can add what you want.
Let's be honest with them and focus on what happens next.
